what: The PDD ladder the 2026-09-03 speedup ladder turned out to need. That ladder rendered PDD8 only as the shipped graph (sage auto plus Sol at the PDD window) and it lost to the true baseline on every scene; the owner pointed out that no arm rendered PDD8 without Sol or without sage, so the loss attributes to nothing narrower than the shipped graph (bench/results/2026-09-04_ladder_2026-09-03_verdict.json, owner_report_after_join). The owner's ask on 2026-09-04: PDD without Sol at 8 steps, and PDD with Sol at more conservative settings. Same five scenes, same seed, 1344x768, 345 frames; judged blind against each other and against the ladder's dense 16-step clips.

scenes.standoff: t2va_frontier_standoff -- see bench/ladder_arms.json for what each scene tests
scenes.diner: t2va_diner_breakup -- see bench/ladder_arms.json for what each scene tests
scenes.opera: t2va_opera_grand_stage -- see bench/ladder_arms.json for what each scene tests
scenes.stairwell: t2va_stairwell_dialogue -- see bench/ladder_arms.json for what each scene tests
scenes.subway: t2va_subway_chase -- see bench/ladder_arms.json for what each scene tests

rungs.pdd8sage: PDD8 with sage auto on every step and Sol absent (h3_probe_t2v_pdd8_sage). The owner's 'pdd without sol'. Listed first: it answers the primary question on its own.
rungs.pdd8sol2: the shipped PDD8 graph with Sol's window narrowed by two patches, start_percent 0.3 and end_percent 0.6. At shift 12 that leaves Sol sparse on two of the eight steps (the ones at sigma 0.952 and 0.923) instead of the shipped four; the arithmetic is docs/SOLATTN.md's sigma-window section, and the choice is REASONED from it (dense warm-up steps set structure, the coarsest block runs dense), not measured. The owner's 'sol at better settings'.
rungs.pdd8sol4: the shipped PDD8 graph unpatched (h3_text_to_video_pdd_api): sage auto plus Sol at the PDD-specific window, sparse on four of eight. Re-rendered here rather than reused from the ladder so every PDD rung comes from one server process and one execution regime.
rungs.pdd8dense: PDD8 under ComfyUI's stock attention, neither sage nor Sol (h3_probe_t2v_pdd8_dense): the PDD ladder's own baseline and the vendor's reference configuration. A control, not a candidate, and slow (docs/h3_pdd.md: dense attention at this length costs more per step than sage plus Sol). Listed last so a run can stop before it.

prompts: named by bank id through the runner's @bank: value; the text lives only in prompt_bank/
reference_rows: the quality reference is the ladder's dense 16-step clip per scene: the rows labelled <scene>_dense in bench/results/2026-09-03_ladder_arms_judged.jsonl. Append those five rows to this run's JSONL before blinding so blind_batch.py can pair them by run index. They were rendered on 2026-09-03 on a server started before the ComfyUI pull of 2026-09-04 (which turned the compiler malloc graph on), so every pair against them is cross-regime until a dense rung re-rendered after the pull is shown pixel-identical to its 2026-09-03 clip; a peer session was asked to make that render on 2026-09-04.
run: python bench/run_graph_arms.py --manifest bench/pdd_ladder_arms.json --runs 1 --seed 730451892 --hold-seed --no-alternate --warmup standoff_pdd8sage --out bench/results/<date>_pdd_ladder_arms.jsonl; append the five dense rows named above; then bench/blind_batch.py on that JSONL with, per scene, --pairs <scene>_pdd8sage,<scene>_pdd8sol4 --pairs <scene>_pdd8sage,<scene>_pdd8sol2 --pairs <scene>_dense,<scene>_pdd8sage --pairs <scene>_dense,<scene>_pdd8sol2 and, if pdd8dense rendered, --pairs <scene>_pdd8dense,<scene>_pdd8sage; score pairs AND singles; bench/score_session.py.

pairs_that_are_controlled.pdd8sage vs pdd8sol4: Sol's effect on the PDD8 schedule at the shipped window; same graph family, same steps, same seed. The primary question.
pairs_that_are_controlled.pdd8sage vs pdd8sol2: whether a narrower window recovers what the shipped window loses, if it loses anything
pairs_that_are_controlled.dense (ladder, 16 steps) vs pdd8sage: is PDD8 without Sol as good as the true baseline; cross-regime, see reference_rows
pairs_that_are_controlled.dense (ladder, 16 steps) vs pdd8sol2: the fastest arm that might pass, against the baseline; cross-regime
pairs_that_are_controlled.pdd8dense vs pdd8sage: sage's effect on the PDD8 schedule; only if pdd8dense rendered

how_to_read: within a scene only, never across scenes. The ladder's reading rules apply unchanged: one seed per arm, so each contest is one stack judged once; every contest in a scene shares one clip per rung, so a rung that loses twice lost on one clip and one defect. Score the singles this time: the ladder's audio half exists only as the owner's verbal report, and bench/measure_clip_loudness.py on this run's outputs record puts a level beside whatever the owner hears.
cost: reasoned, not measured: bench/results/2026-09-03_ladder_outputs.json carries the ladder's per-arm sampler times, from which a sage step and a Sol step each have a median; pdd8sage is eight sage steps, pdd8sol2 six sage plus two Sol, pdd8sol4 four plus four, pdd8dense eight steps at the dense rung's per-step cost. Any timing taken after the 2026-09-04 ComfyUI pull is in a new execution regime and is not comparable to that record.
requires: a ComfyUI server up with this pack's graphs regenerated. The two probe graphs were built with --no-validate on a stopped server on 2026-09-04; run workflows/build_workflows.py against the live /object_info before the first render.
generated_by: workflows/build_workflows.py for the two probe graphs; regenerate there, never edit the graphs
